market_context: U.S. futures and premarket ETFs indicate a risk-off open: S&P 500 futures were down roughly 0.3%-0.4%, Nasdaq futures were down 0.1%-0.2%, and Dow futures were down about 0.6%-0.7%.[3][5] The prior session's AI-led selloff, oil above $100, and concerns about AI spending remain the dominant pressures, although some semiconductor names were showing modest premarket stabilization.[2][4][9]

predictions.reasoning: S&P 500 futures were down approximately 0.3%-0.4% before the open, while the prior session saw the S&P 500 fall 1.21%.[3][5] Elevated oil prices and ongoing AI-spending concerns favor continued pressure, though the recent selloff may limit the magnitude of the decline.

Nasdaq futures were modestly lower after the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.6% and major AI stocks sold off sharply in the prior session.[2][3] The technology-heavy index remains more exposed than the broader market to valuation and AI-capital-spending concerns.

Nvidia fell about 4.4% in the prior session amid broad AI-trade liquidation.[2][10] Modest premarket stabilization in selected semiconductor names could cushion the decline, so the expected move is smaller than Thursday's selloff.

Meta plunged 7% during the prior session as investors questioned the sustainability of very large AI spending commitments.[2] With futures still weak and risk appetite pressured by oil above $100, a full-day rebound appears less likely than additional consolidation.

Dow futures were down approximately 0.6%-0.7% before the open despite the Dow's marginal gain in the prior session.[3][5] The index may outperform technology-heavy benchmarks, but broad risk-off positioning and higher oil prices still imply a modest decline.
